rows.ARS:
White, near white or white blend Hybrid Tea.
Registration name: Garden Party (hybrid tea, Swim, 1959)
rows.Origin:
Bred by Herbert C. Swim (United States, before 1958).
Introduced in France by Jean-Marie Gaujard in 1959 as 'Garden Party'.
Introduced in United States by Armstrong Roses in 1959 as 'Garden Party'.
Introduced by Unknown (Australia) in 1960 as 'Garden Party'.
rows.Bloom: Cream, pink edges. Flowers pale yellow to white, often tinged with light pink, Nasturtium fragrance. Mild fragrance. 28 petals. Average diameter 4.75". Very large, full (26-40 petals), high-centered bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Habit:
Large, dark green foliage.

Height: 3' to 6'7" (90 to 200cm). Width: 2' (60cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 7b and warmer. Can be used for cut flower or garden. Disease susceptibility: susceptible to Mildew. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that. Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) .
rows.Patents: United States - Patent No: PP 1,814 on 3 Mar 1959 VIEW USPTO PATENT
rows.Notes: Nigel Pratt of Tasman Bay Roses says this rose has creamy-white flowers edged with pink...

fragrance: Flowers pale yellow to white, often tinged with light pink, Nasturtium fragrance.
